gate.title: Is this server yours?
gate.lede: When the backend starts for the first time and the site has no owner yet, it prints a setup code to its log. Open the link from the log, or paste the code here.
gate.logLooksLike: You'll see a line like this
gate.badCode: That code isn't right. After 10 wrong tries a new one is issued, so check the log again.
gate.envHint: If OWNER_EMAIL is set in .env.backend you won't see this page: whoever signs in with that address is the owner.

owner.title: Claim the site
owner.lede: The admin only takes GitHub or Google sign-in. Whichever account you sign in with and claim the site from becomes its owner.
owner.claimed: Claimed. Next: languages, the site name and which pages to show. All of it can be changed in the admin later.
owner.noneConfigured: Neither GitHub nor Google sign-in is set up yet, and at least one is needed to get into the admin. Follow the steps for either one below, restart the backend, then reload this page. The setup code stays the same.
owner.oneMore: You can add the other one later; readers get one more way to sign in when they comment.
owner.siteUrl: This site's address is {{url}} (SITE_URL in .env). If that's wrong, fix it before setting up sign-in, or you'll be sent to the wrong place after signing in.

errors.bad_code: The setup code is wrong or has been replaced. Go back to the first step and enter it again.
errors.already_claimed: This site already has an owner.
errors.not_signed_in: Your sign-in has expired. Please sign in again.

github.title: Set up GitHub sign-in
github.s1: Open GitHub's "New OAuth App" page (Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps → New OAuth App):
github.s2: Fill it in as below. The application name can be anything; the site name works:
github.s3: Click Register application. On the app's page, copy the Client ID, then click "Generate a new client secret" and copy that too (it's only shown once).
github.s4: On the server, open .env.backend and fill in both values:
github.s5: Restart the backend so it picks them up, then reload this page:

google.title: Set up Google sign-in
google.s1: Open Google Auth Platform in the Google Cloud Console (it asks you to create a project first if you don't have one):
google.s2: The first time, it asks for some basics: use the site name as the app name, your own address as the support email, and choose "External" for the audience.
google.s3: If the publishing status stays at "Testing", add your own Google account as a test user under Audience, or the sign-in will be blocked.
google.s4: Under Clients, click "Create client", choose "Web application" and fill it in as below:
google.s5: Once it's created, copy the client ID and client secret, then open .env.backend on the server and fill them in:
google.s6: Restart the backend so it picks them up, then reload this page:

lang.title: Languages
lang.lede: Readers see the default language at the plain address; every other language gets its own prefix.

site.title: Site
site.lede: Shown on the home page, in the RSS feed and on share cards. All of it can be changed in the admin later.

pages.title: Pages
pages.lede: The chart is your home page. A page you turn off takes its orbit with it, and you can turn it back on in the admin any time.

done.title: You're live
done.lede: There's no content yet, so readers see quiet empty pages. Fill them in under Pages in the admin.

closed.title: This site is already set up
closed.lede: It already has an owner, so first-time setup won't open again. The owner signs in to the admin from the site with GitHub or Google.
